text: For my project on invertebrates, I chose to study tardigrades.
translation: 为了我关于无脊椎动物的项目，我选择研究缓步动物。

text: These are microscopic - or to be more precise - near-microscopic animals.
translation: 这些是微观的——或者更准确地说——接近微观的动物。

text: There are well over a thousand known species of these tiny animals, which belong to the phylum Tardigrada.
translation: 这些微小动物已知的物种远超过一千种，它们属于缓步动物门。

text: Most tardigrades range in length from 0.05 to 1 millimetre, though the largest species can grow to be 1.2 millimetres in length.
translation: 大多数缓步动物的体长在0.05到1毫米之间，不过最大的物种可以长到1.2毫米长。

text: They are also sometimes called 'water bears': 'water' because that's where they thrive best and 'bear' because of the way they move.
translation: 它们有时也被称为“水熊”：“水”是因为那是它们生长得最好的地方，“熊”是因为它们移动的方式。

text: 'Moss piglet' is another name for tardigrades because of the way they look when viewed from the front.
translation: “苔藓小猪”是缓步动物的另一个名字，因为从正面看它们的样子像小猪。

text: They were first discovered in Germany in 1773 by Johann Goeze, who coined the name Tardigrada.
translation: 它们最早于1773年在德国由约翰·戈泽发现，他创造了Tardigrada这个名字。

text: As I say, there are many different species of tardigrade - too many to describe here - but, generally speaking, the different species share similar physical traits.
translation: 正如我所说，缓步动物有许多不同的物种——多到无法在这里一一描述——但一般来说，不同物种具有相似的体貌特征。

text: They have a body which is short, and also rounded - a bit like a barrel - and the body comprises four segments.
translation: 它们的身体短而圆——有点像桶——身体由四个节段组成。

text: Each segment has a pair of legs, at the end of which are between four and eight sharp claws.
translation: 每个节段有一对腿，腿的末端有四到八只锋利的爪子。

text: I should also say that some species don't have any claws; what they have are discs, and these work by means of suction.
translation: 我还应该说明，有些物种没有任何爪子；它们拥有的是圆盘，而这些圆盘通过吸力起作用。

text: They enable the tardigrade to cling on to surfaces or to grip its prey.
translation: 它们使缓步动物能够附着在表面上或抓住猎物。

text: Within the body, there are no lungs, or any organs for breathing at all.
translation: 在身体内部，没有肺，也完全没有用于呼吸的任何器官。

text: Instead, oxygen and also blood are transported in a fluid that fills the cavity of the body.
translation: 相反，氧气以及血液是在一种充满身体腔体的液体中被输送的。

text: As far as the tardigrade's head is concerned, the best way I can describe this is that it looks rather strange - a bit squashed even - though many of the websites I looked at described its appearance as cute, which isn't exactly very scientific.
translation: 就缓步动物的头部而言，我能描述它的最好方式是它看起来相当奇怪——甚至有点被压扁了——尽管我看过的许多网站把它的外观描述为可爱，这并不十分科学。

text: The tardigrade's mouth is a kind of tube that can open outwards to reveal teeth-like structures known as 'stylets'.
translation: 缓步动物的嘴是一种管状结构，可以向外张开，露出被称为“口针”的类似牙齿的结构。

text: These are sharp enough to pierce plant or animal cells.
translation: 它们足够锋利，可以刺穿植物或动物细胞。

text: So where are tardigrades found?
translation: 那么，缓步动物在哪里被发现呢？

text: Well, they live in every part of the world, in a variety of habitats: most commonly, on the bed of a lake, or on many kinds of plants or in very wet environments.
translation: 嗯，它们生活在世界的每一个角落，栖息地多种多样：最常见的是在湖底，或在许多种类的植物上，或在非常潮湿的环境中。

text: There's been some interesting research which has found that tardigrades are capable of surviving radiation and very high pressure, and they're also able to withstand temperatures as cold as - 200 degrees centigrade, or highs of more than 148 degrees centigrade, which is incredibly hot.
translation: 有一些有趣的研究发现，缓步动物能够经受住辐射和非常高的压力，它们也能承受低至零下200摄氏度或高达148摄氏度以上的温度，这热得令人难以置信。

text: It has been said that tardigrades could survive long after human beings have been wiped out, even in the event of an asteroid hitting the earth.
translation: 据说，缓步动物在人类灭绝很久之后仍能存活，即使发生小行星撞击地球的事件也不例外。

text: If conditions become too extreme and tardigrades are at risk of drying out, they enter a state called cryptobiosis.
translation: 如果环境变得过于极端，缓步动物面临脱水的危险，它们就会进入一种叫做隐生的状态。

text: They curl into a ball, called a tun - that's T-U-N - by retracting their head and legs, and their metabolism drops to less than one percent of normal levels.
translation: 它们会缩成一个球，叫做 tun——拼写是 T-U-N——方法是缩回头部和腿部，新陈代谢降到正常水平的百分之一以下。

text: They can remain like this until they are re-introduced to water, when they will come back to life in a matter of a few hours.
translation: 它们可以一直保持这种状态，直到重新接触到水，那时它们会在几个小时内复活。
highlights: in a matter of a few hours

text: While in a state of cryptobiosis, tardigrades produce a protein that protects their DNA.
translation: 在隐生状态下，缓步动物会产生一种保护其 DNA 的蛋白质。
highlights: While in a state of cryptobiosis

text: In 2016, scientists revived two tardigrades that had been tuns for more than 30 years.
translation: 2016 年，科学家使两只已经处于 tun 状态超过 30 年的缓步动物复活了。

text: There was a report that, in 1948, a 120-year-old tun was revived, but this experiment has never been repeated.
translation: 有报道称，1948 年一只 120 岁的 tun 被复活了，但这个实验从未被重复过。

text: There are currently several tests taking place in space, to determine how long tardigrades might be able to survive there.
translation: 目前有几项测试正在太空中进行，以确定缓步动物能在那里存活多久。

text: I believe the record so far is 10 days.
translation: 我相信到目前为止的纪录是 10 天。

text: So, erm, moving on.
translation: 那么，呃，我们继续吧。

text: In terms of their diet, tardigrades consume liquids in order to survive.
translation: 在饮食方面，缓步动物靠摄入液体来生存。

text: Although they have teeth, they don't use these for chewing.
translation: 尽管它们有牙齿，但并不用牙齿来咀嚼。

text: They suck the juices from moss, or extract fluid from seaweed, but some species prey on other tardigrades, from other species or within their own.
translation: 它们从苔藓中吸取汁液，或从海藻中提取液体，但有些物种会捕食其他缓步动物，包括其他物种的或同种内的。

text: I suppose this isn't surprising, given that tardigrades are mainly comprised of liquid and are coated with a type of gel.
translation: 我觉得这并不令人意外，因为缓步动物主要由液体构成，并且表面覆盖着一层凝胶。

text: Finally, I'd like to mention the conservation status of tardigrades.
translation: 最后，我想提一下缓步动物的保护状况。

text: It is estimated that they have been in existence for approximately half a billion years and, in that time, they have survived five mass extinctions.
translation: 据估计，它们已经存在了大约五亿年，在这段时间里，它们经历了五次大灭绝。

text: So, it will probably come as no surprise to you, that tardigrades have not been evaluated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and are not on any endangered list.
translation: 所以，你们可能不会感到意外：缓步动物尚未被国际自然保护联盟评估，也不在任何濒危名录上。
highlights: International Union for Conservation of Nature

text: Some researchers have described them as thriving.
translation: 一些研究人员称它们正在蓬勃发展。

text: Does anyone have any questions they'd like to ask?
translation: 有人有问题想问吗？
